brief: Today's posts centered on new model and product releases, including Gemini 4 Neon compared with Opus 5.5 and ChatGPT's new mobile experience. Beyond that, several builders reacted to Anthropic's success and to ongoing infrastructure attacks.

themes.label: Gemini 4 Neon vs Opus 5.5
themes.summary: Peter Yang tested Gemini 4 Neon against Opus 5.5, finding Neon on par or better for writing and faster than Carbon, while Opus is still stronger at 3D and design.

themes.label: Agents as workflow infrastructure
themes.summary: Builders described agents as infrastructure: Vercel's Board as a headless state layer for agent factories, agent contracts, and personal agents built from one prompt.

themes.label: ChatGPT mobile redesign
themes.summary: Thibault Sottiaux announced a new mobile ChatGPT experience with a dedicated tab, starting with Pro users, and asked for feedback before wider rollout.

builders.name: Guillermo Rauch
builders.summary: Argued that Vercel's Board is infrastructure for agents, with UI now cheap to generate, and posted a view that coding engineers gain outsized leverage. Also posted that a company's genesis is the agent that helps build it.

builders.name: Peter Yang
builders.summary: Compared Gemini 4 Neon with Opus 5.5 in a video, finding Neon strong for writing and speed, and recommended the Gemini Ultra subscription. Other posts were brief comparisons and a note on Google's employee testing.

builders.name: Aditya Agarwal
builders.summary: Congratulated Anthropic and explained SPC's role in its founding through two members. Also highlighted RoleCUA from Fig, a dataset mapping expert roles across months of work.

builders.name: Amjad Masad
builders.summary: Shared a way to build a Muse-like personal agent with one prompt and said agent contracts are a paradigm others will copy. Other posts were short reactions.

builders.name: No Priors
builders.summary: Released a podcast episode with Bob McGrew, CEO and co-founder of Arda, on why superintelligence needs the physical world and on American manufacturing.

builders.name: Josh Woodward
builders.summary: Announced that the Gemini app on Mac can now perform tasks on the user's computer, a top feature request.

builders.name: Peter Steinberger
builders.summary: Said he landed a fix in OpenClaw for users of the embedded harness, noting most harnesses are not yet updated.

builders.name: Thibault Sottiaux
builders.summary: Announced a new mobile ChatGPT experience with a pinnable tab for Pro users and said the team is aiming to improve the experience used by 1.2B users in place.

builders.name: Thariq
builders.summary: Argued that software is both art and utility and that AI is both an Industrial Revolution and a Renaissance. Other posts were minimal.

builders.name: Claude
builders.summary: Posted three link-only updates with no accompanying text.

builders.name: Swyx
builders.summary: Criticized hyperbolic social media predictions about SOTA with no consequences for inaccuracy. Other posts were brief reactions.

builders.name: Garry Tan
builders.summary: Posted a short agreement with Bostrom's view that if nobody builds it, everyone dies.

builders.name: Matt Turck
builders.summary: Shared a conversation with Felix Rieseberg of Anthropic. Other posts were short reactions.

builders.name: Nikunj Kothari
builders.summary: Proposed four layers where security for elderly users against scams and impersonation could work, from browser to payments. Other posts were brief reactions.

builders.name: Dan Shipper
builders.summary: Asked who is working to stop the infrastructure attacks happening now and how people in AI can help.
